about.title: About
about.description: About Teo Furlan: from a computer in 2004 to agents and a robot arm in 2026.
paragraphs: I'm a software developer at Universidad Adventista del Plata, where I started Information Systems Engineering in 2022. I build software with AI agents: Socra, a local voice layer for any coding agent or harness, and a harness that tracks every task I give the agent. I'm based in Entre Ríos, Argentina, and open to remote work.

The hardware side started at a technical secondary school, in electromechanical equipment and installations. During college I built several projects; one of them is EmprendER, an entrepreneurship platform. In 2026, in a team of 3, I'm building a low-cost robot arm for laparoscopic surgery training.

ai.title: How I build with AI
ai.description: The harness around the agent: a workflow that tracks every task, a learning vault, project exams and memory.
ai.heading: The harness around the agent
ai.lead: I do not just prompt an agent. I run it inside a harness: a workflow that tracks every task, a learning vault, project exams and memory.
ai.figureAria: Diagram of the harness. A loop runs from request to feature doc to agent to checks to commit and back to request. The learning vault, exams and memory are side blocks attached to the agent.
ai.figureCaption: FIG. 3.1 · The harness around the agent. Schematic.
parts: A workflow that tracks every task

sections.heading: A workflow that tracks every task
sections.html: I call it Organic Driven Development (ODD). Every request is authorized, explored and sized before any code changes. Larger work gets a feature document in the repo, odd/tasks/<feature>.md, with numbered specs that quote my request verbatim, a task table and a log. The agent then works task by task, test-first where it applies, commits reviewable work units, and reports what was verified and what was not. Push, pull requests and publishing stay my decision. The build session for this site shows it in practice.

sections.heading: A learning vault
sections.html: An Obsidian vault holds learning notes, kept per project. Each project runs in one of three modes: learn, log or off. Conceptual questions become concept notes. The vault never copies repo docs, so it stays a record of what I learned, not a second copy of the code.

sections.heading: Project exams
sections.html: At milestones the agent writes an open-answer exam about the project and grades my answers. The point is simple: I should be able to explain the code the agent helped write.

sections.heading: Memory
sections.html: Engram, a persistent memory, saves decisions, bug fixes and discoveries across sessions. After a break or a context compaction, the work can resume where it stopped.

ai.closingHtml: I wrote about the learning part in more detail: How I Built a Learning System Inside My AI Coding Workflow (Using Obsidian) on DEV.

colophon.title: Colophon
colophon.description: How teofurlan.com is built, and the tooling credits.
stack: Astro 7, built to static pages and served from Cloudflare Workers static assets.
Type: IBM Plex Sans and IBM Plex Mono, self-hosted.
Images are resized and stripped of metadata at build time with Sharp.
Two themes, dark blueprint and light paper. They follow your system setting until you pick one.
Works without JavaScript. Scripts only add the theme toggle, the drafting-grid pointer, the scroll drawings and the email link.
colophon.toolingHtml: Built with the gentle-ai harness and AI Hero skills. The whole build conversation with the coding agent is on How this site was built.
